benchmark.exact_method: import origin.py without main; call actual Origin.snapshot on SimpleNamespace with identical cumulative body bytearray/header/certificate fields after each captured chunk size
benchmark.limits: Pure algorithm only. Does not measure actual stdout pipeblocking, runner diskflush, UDPcrypto/ACKs, event-loop scheduling or contestedCPUload. No live test or deadlines changed.

supported_findings: origin.py34-43 snapshot copies body bytearray to bytes and recomputes SHA256 of entire accumulated body. DATA callback91-94 synchronously invokes snapshot+emit(flush=True) every event on aioquic event-loop thread.

627 tiny DATA events for1MiB imply337,047,994 cumulativebytes copied+hashed before echo response allocation. Exact on-interpreter snapshot+json algorithm costs median1.388s, about27.8percent of original5sdeadline; this is algorithm benchmark, not measured wire-time breakdown.

An incremental SHA256 hasher updated per DATA chunk and snapshot using bytearray length avoids cumulative hashing. Every627captured cumulativedigest is identical in independent pure comparison; exact count/FIN/finalhash assertions can remain unchanged. Retain bodybytearray for exact echoedresponse.

origin uses stdout print(flush=True); runner readerthread immediately reads eachline, writes logfile+flush then enqueues JSON. Originlog is310754bytes. Blocking pipe/disk costs are possible but neither pipe occupancy nor per-write timing is captured; cannot assert they are causal.

No pause_upload/resume_upload control was reached in this failing run. /tiny-upload begins echo response only after full requestFIN; uploadsnapshots cost therefore belongs preceding upload phase of same original totaldeadline. There is no snapshot/hash work on responseDATA sends after thatFIN.
